data.title: A masked, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial evaluating safety and the effect on cardiac function of low-dose rapamycin in 17 healthy client-owned dogs
data.authors: Barnett BG; Kaeberlein M; Creevy KE

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Companion dogs (client-owned, RCT, n=17, ages 6-10 y)
data.finding: In 17 healthy pet dogs, 6 months of low-dose rapamycin (0.025 mg/kg, three times a week) caused no clinically significant adverse events. Echocardiography, however, showed NO statistically significant difference from placebo at 6 or 12 months, so the heart benefit hinted at in the earlier 10-week trial (URF2017) was not reproduced. Owners did report perceived positive changes in behavior or health more often in the rapamycin group (26.8% vs 8.1% of bi-weekly surveys), but that is a subjective, owner-reported outcome. A small safety-focused trial, not designed to test lifespan.
data.abstract_excerpt: Geroscience studies of low-dose rapamycin in laboratory species have identified numerous benefits, including reversing age-related cardiac dysfunction. Cardiovascular benefits have been observed in dogs with 10 weeks of treatment, raising questions about possible benefits and adverse effects of long-term use of low-dose rapamycin. The objectives of this study were to assess the impact of 6 months of low-dose rapamycin on echocardiographic indices of cardiac function in healthy dogs and to document the occurrence of adverse events.

extracted_findings.intervention: Rapamycin 0.025 mg/kg three times per week for 6 months vs placebo
extracted_findings.effect: Well tolerated for 6 months, but no measurable change in heart function versus placebo (small trial)
